claim: Semaphorin 3F (Sema3F) and semaphorin 3A (Sema3A) exhibit remarkably distinct effects on deep layer excitatory cortical pyramidal neurons.
source: Secreted semaphorin 3F (Sema3F) and semaphorin 3A (Sema3A) exhibit remarkably distinct effects on deep layer excitatory cortical pyramidal neurons; Sema3F mediates dendritic spine pruning, whereas Sema3A promotes the elaboration of basal dendrites.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to prior work (Tran et al., 2009) and experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Sema3F mediates dendritic spine pruning in deep layer cortical pyramidal neurons.
source: Secreted semaphorin 3F (Sema3F) and semaphorin 3A (Sema3A) exhibit remarkably distinct effects on deep layer excitatory cortical pyramidal neurons; Sema3F mediates dendritic spine pruning, whereas Sema3A promotes the elaboration of basal dendrites.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in the manuscript and citations to prior work (Tran et al., 2009).

claim: Sema3A promotes the elaboration of basal dendrites in deep layer cortical pyramidal neurons.
source: Secreted semaphorin 3F (Sema3F) and semaphorin 3A (Sema3A) exhibit remarkably distinct effects on deep layer excitatory cortical pyramidal neurons; Sema3F mediates dendritic spine pruning, whereas Sema3A promotes the elaboration of basal dendrites.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in the manuscript and citations to prior work (Tran et al., 2009).

claim: Sema3F and Sema3A signal through distinct holoreceptors that include neuropilin-2 (Nrp2)/plexinA3 (PlexA3) and neuropilin-1 (Nrp1)/PlexA4, respectively.
source: Sema3F and Sema3A signal through distinct holoreceptors that include neuropilin-2 (Nrp2)/plexinA3 (PlexA3) and neuropilin-1 (Nrp1)/PlexA4, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citation to prior work (Yaron et al., 2005).

claim: Nrp2 and Nrp1 are S-palmitoylated in cortical neurons.
source: We find that Nrp2 and Nrp1 are S-palmitoylated in cortical neurons and that palmitoylation of select Nrp2 cysteines is required for its proper subcellular localization, cell surface clustering, and also for Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent dendritic spine pruning in cortical neurons, both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by acyl-biotin exchange (ABE) assay data presented in Figure 2B and 2C.

claim: Palmitoylation of select Nrp2 cysteines is required for proper subcellular localization of Nrp2.
source: We find that Nrp2 and Nrp1 are S-palmitoylated in cortical neurons and that palmitoylation of select Nrp2 cysteines is required for its proper subcellular localization, cell surface clustering, and also for Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent dendritic spine pruning in cortical neurons, both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing mislocalization of Nrp2 CS mutants in Figures 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Palmitoylation of select Nrp2 cysteines is required for cell surface clustering of Nrp2.
source: We find that Nrp2 and Nrp1 are S-palmitoylated in cortical neurons and that palmitoylation of select Nrp2 cysteines is required for its proper subcellular localization, cell surface clustering, and also for Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent dendritic spine pruning in cortical neurons, both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing altered clustering of Nrp2 CS mutants in Figures 1, 3, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Palmitoylation of select Nrp2 cysteines is required for Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent dendritic spine pruning in cortical neurons in vitro.
source: We find that Nrp2 and Nrp1 are S-palmitoylated in cortical neurons and that palmitoylation of select Nrp2 cysteines is required for its proper subcellular localization, cell surface clustering, and also for Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent dendritic spine pruning in cortical neurons, both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by rescue experiments in Nrp2-/- cortical neurons shown in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Palmitoylation of select Nrp2 cysteines is required for Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent dendritic spine pruning in cortical neurons in vivo.
source: We find that Nrp2 and Nrp1 are S-palmitoylated in cortical neurons and that palmitoylation of select Nrp2 cysteines is required for its proper subcellular localization, cell surface clustering, and also for Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent dendritic spine pruning in cortical neurons, both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by in utero electroporation rescue experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: The palmitoyl acyltransferase ZDHHC15 is required for Nrp2 palmitoylation.
source: Moreover, we show that the palmitoyl acyltransferase ZDHHC15 is required for Nrp2 palmitoylation and Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent dendritic spine pruning, but it is dispensable for Nrp1 palmitoylation and Sema3A/Nrp1-dependent basal dendritic elaboration.
evidence: This claim is supported by ABE assay data in Zdhhc15-KO cortical neurons shown in Figure 6A and 6B.

claim: ZDHHC15 is required for Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent dendritic spine pruning.
source: Moreover, we show that the palmitoyl acyltransferase ZDHHC15 is required for Nrp2 palmitoylation and Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent dendritic spine pruning, but it is dispensable for Nrp1 palmitoylation and Sema3A/Nrp1-dependent basal dendritic elaboration.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing loss of Sema3F-induced spine pruning in Zdhhc15-KO neurons in Figure 6D-F and in vivo data in Figure 7A-B.

claim: ZDHHC15 is dispensable for Nrp1 palmitoylation.
source: Moreover, we show that the palmitoyl acyltransferase ZDHHC15 is required for Nrp2 palmitoylation and Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent dendritic spine pruning, but it is dispensable for Nrp1 palmitoylation and Sema3A/Nrp1-dependent basal dendritic elaboration.
evidence: This claim is supported by ABE assay data showing no change in Nrp1 palmitoylation in Zdhhc15-KO neurons in Figure 6A and 6C.

claim: ZDHHC15 is dispensable for Sema3A/Nrp1-dependent basal dendritic elaboration.
source: Moreover, we show that the palmitoyl acyltransferase ZDHHC15 is required for Nrp2 palmitoylation and Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent dendritic spine pruning, but it is dispensable for Nrp1 palmitoylation and Sema3A/Nrp1-dependent basal dendritic elaboration.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing normal Sema3A-induced dendritic elaboration in Zdhhc15-KO neurons in Figure 6G-I and normal dendritic arborization in vivo in Figure 7C-D.

claim: Palmitoyl acyltransferase-substrate specificity is essential for establishing compartmentalized neuronal structure and functional responses to extrinsic guidance cues.
source: Therefore, palmitoyl acyltransferase-substrate specificity is essential for establishing compartmentalized neuronal structure and functional responses to extrinsic guidance cues.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing differential effects of ZDHHC15 on Nrp2 versus Nrp1 function.

claim: Nrp2 is distributed on the COS-7 cell surface in a clustered pattern consisting of numerous discrete puncta.
source: We observed that Nrp2 is distributed on the COS-7 cell surface in a clustered pattern consisting of numerous discrete puncta (Figure 1A), whereas Nrp1 is evenly distributed over the entire plasma membrane with little evidence of clustering (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by surface staining data shown in Figure 1A and quantified in Figure 1C.

claim: Nrp1 is evenly distributed over the entire plasma membrane with little evidence of clustering in COS-7 cells.
source: We observed that Nrp2 is distributed on the COS-7 cell surface in a clustered pattern consisting of numerous discrete puncta (Figure 1A), whereas Nrp1 is evenly distributed over the entire plasma membrane with little evidence of clustering (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by surface staining data shown in Figure 1B and quantified in Figure 1C.

claim: Treatment with 2-bromopalmitate causes Nrp2 to be markedly redistributed to a diffuse localization on the cell surface similar to Nrp1.
source: Following bath application of 2-bromopalmitate, Nrp2 was markedly redistributed compared to the control, displaying a diffuse localization on the cell surface similar to Nrp1, which is localized diffusely following either control or 2-bromopalmitate treatment (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and quantified in Figure 1E.

claim: Nrp1 localization is not affected by 2-bromopalmitate treatment.
source: Following bath application of 2-bromopalmitate, Nrp2 was markedly redistributed compared to the control, displaying a diffuse localization on the cell surface similar to Nrp1, which is localized diffusely following either control or 2-bromopalmitate treatment (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and quantified in Figure 1E.

claim: Protein palmitoylation is required for Nrp2 cell surface clustering in heterologous cells in vitro.
source: These results show that Nrp2 and Nrp1 exhibit distinct cell surface compartmental localization and that protein palmitoylation is required for Nrp2 cell surface clustering in heterologous cells in vitro.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the 2-bromopalmitate experiments shown in Figure 1D-E.

claim: Both Nrp2 and Nrp1 harbor cysteine residues in their transmembrane and membrane-proximal (juxtamembrane) domains.
source: Both Nrp2 and Nrp1 harbor cysteine residues in their transmembrane and membrane-proximal (juxtamembrane) domains (Figure 2A, in red).
evidence: This is shown in the amino acid sequence alignment in Figure 2A.

claim: Nrp2 has a lone cysteine residue, C897, carboxy-terminal to the transmembrane domain.
source: Nrp2 also has a lone cysteine residue, C897 (Figure 2A, in red) carboxy-terminal (C-terminal) to the transmembrane domain and two adjacent C-terminal cysteine residues (Figure 2A, in blue).
evidence: This is shown in the amino acid sequence in Figure 2A.

claim: Nrp2 has two adjacent C-terminal cysteine residues.
source: Nrp2 also has a lone cysteine residue, C897 (Figure 2A, in red) carboxy-terminal (C-terminal) to the transmembrane domain and two adjacent C-terminal cysteine residues (Figure 2A, in blue).
evidence: This is shown in the amino acid sequence in Figure 2A.

claim: Nrp2 and Nrp1 cysteine residues are highly phylogenetically conserved among vertebrate species.
source: These Nrp2 and Nrp1 cysteine residues are all highly phylogenetically conserved among vertebrate species (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in the cross-species amino acid sequence alignment in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both Nrp2 and Nrp1 are palmitoylated in adult mouse forebrain.
source: We observed that both Nrp2 and Nrp1 are palmitoylated in adult mouse forebrain and in embryonic day 14.5 (E14.5) mouse cerebral cortex (Figure 2B), as are both Nrps in cortical neurons 28 days in vitro (DIV) derived from E14.5 embryos (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ABE assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Both Nrp2 and Nrp1 are palmitoylated in embryonic day 14.5 (E14.5) mouse cerebral cortex.
source: We observed that both Nrp2 and Nrp1 are palmitoylated in adult mouse forebrain and in embryonic day 14.5 (E14.5) mouse cerebral cortex (Figure 2B), as are both Nrps in cortical neurons 28 days in vitro (DIV) derived from E14.5 embryos (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ABE assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Both Nrp2 and Nrp1 are palmitoylated in cortical neurons 28 days in vitro (DIV) derived from E14.5 embryos.
source: We observed that both Nrp2 and Nrp1 are palmitoylated in adult mouse forebrain and in embryonic day 14.5 (E14.5) mouse cerebral cortex (Figure 2B), as are both Nrps in cortical neurons 28 days in vitro (DIV) derived from E14.5 embryos (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ABE assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Nrp2 is palmitoylated on all transmembrane and membrane-proximal cysteines, albeit to variable extents.
source: This analysis revealed that Nrp2 is palmitoylated on all transmembrane and membrane-proximal cysteines, albeit to variable extents, as well as on the C-terminal di-cysteine motif (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by ABE assay data on Nrp2 CS mutants shown in Figure 2D and 2E.

claim: Nrp2 is palmitoylated on the C-terminal di-cysteine motif.
source: This analysis revealed that Nrp2 is palmitoylated on all transmembrane and membrane-proximal cysteines, albeit to variable extents, as well as on the C-terminal di-cysteine motif (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by ABE assay data on Nrp2 CS mutants shown in Figure 2D and 2E.

claim: The cysteine residue C878 is a major Nrp2 palmitate acceptor site.
source: The cysteine residue C878 stands out as a major Nrp2 palmitate acceptor site.
evidence: This is shown in the quantification of palmitoylation levels of Nrp2 CS mutants in Figure 2E.

claim: The Nrp2 transmembrane and membrane-proximal cysteines are major palmitoylation sites.
source: The Nrp2 transmembrane and membrane-proximal cysteines are major palmitoylation sites.
evidence: This is shown in the quantification of palmitoylation levels of Nrp2 TCS and Full CS mutants in Figure 2G.

claim: Nrp1 is palmitoylated on cysteines C875 and C883.
source: A similar analysis for Nrp1 revealed that Nrp1 is palmitoylated on cysteines C875 and C883, but apparently not on C881 (Figure 2H and I).
evidence: This claim is supported by ABE assay data on Nrp1 CS mutants shown in Figure 2H and 2I.

claim: Nrp1 is apparently not palmitoylated on cysteine C881.
source: A similar analysis for Nrp1 revealed that Nrp1 is palmitoylated on cysteines C875 and C883, but apparently not on C881 (Figure 2H and I).
evidence: This claim is supported by ABE assay data on Nrp1 CS mutants shown in Figure 2H and 2I.

claim: Nrp2 and Nrp1 display similar palmitoylation patterns in their transmembrane and membrane-proximal segments.
source: These results show that Nrp2 and Nrp1 display similar palmitoylation patterns in their transmembrane and membrane-proximal segments, and that Nrp2 also harbors C-terminal palmitoylation sites that are not present in Nrp1.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the ABE assay data on Nrp2 and Nrp1 CS mutants shown in Figure 2.

claim: Nrp2 harbors C-terminal palmitoylation sites that are not present in Nrp1.
source: These results show that Nrp2 and Nrp1 display similar palmitoylation patterns in their transmembrane and membrane-proximal segments, and that Nrp2 also harbors C-terminal palmitoylation sites that are not present in Nrp1.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the ABE assay data on Nrp2 and Nrp1 CS mutants shown in Figure 2.

claim: Localization of Nrp2C922S/C923S is for the most part punctate with little difference from Nrp2WT.
source: This assay revealed that localization of Nrp2C922S/C923S, which lacks the C-terminal di-cysteine motif, is for the most part punctate with little difference from Nrp2WT, whereas Nrp2TCS and Nrp2Full CS proteins are profoundly mislocalized (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–1C), exhibiting a non-patterned distribution over the entire plasma membrane that resembles Nrp1.
evidence: This claim is supported by surface staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Nrp2TCS and Nrp2Full CS proteins are profoundly mislocalized, exhibiting a non-patterned distribution over the entire plasma membrane that resembles Nrp1.
source: This assay revealed that localization of Nrp2C922S/C923S, which lacks the C-terminal di-cysteine motif, is for the most part punctate with little difference from Nrp2WT, whereas Nrp2TCS and Nrp2Full CS proteins are profoundly mislocalized (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–1C), exhibiting a non-patterned distribution over the entire plasma membrane that resembles Nrp1.
evidence: This claim is supported by surface staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Nrp2WT and Nrp2C922S/C923S exhibit a prominent punctate localization along the plasma membrane in cortical neurons.
source: These live imaging assessments of surface protein localization showed that Nrp2WT (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A; Video 1) and Nrp2C922S/C923S (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C) exhibit a prominent punctate localization along the plasma membrane, consistent with their distribution in COS-7 cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and 2C.

claim: Nrp2TCS apparently forms larger protein clusters in cortical neurons.
source: In contrast, Nrp2TCS apparently forms larger protein clusters (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), and Nrp2Full CS is profoundly mislocalized displaying a diffuse distribution over all membranes (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Nrp2Full CS is profoundly mislocalized displaying a diffuse distribution over all membranes in cortical neurons.
source: In contrast, Nrp2TCS apparently forms larger protein clusters (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), and Nrp2Full CS is profoundly mislocalized displaying a diffuse distribution over all membranes (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Endogenous Nrp2 is robustly associated with somatic Golgi and dendritic Golgi cisternae known as Golgi outposts.
source: We stained primary cortical neurons in culture with antibodies directed against Nrp2 and the cis-Golgi marker Golgi matrix protein 130 (GM130), which showed that endogenous Nrp2 is robustly associated with somatic Golgi and dendritic Golgi cisternae known as Golgi outposts (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Nrp2 is enriched in the GM130-positive Golgi fraction from mouse brain.
source: Further, Golgi isolation experiments from mouse brain revealed Nrp2 enrichment in the GM130-positive Golgi fraction (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by Golgi isolation and western blotting data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Nrp2WT and Nrp2C922S/C923S proteins display robust association with Golgi membranes.
source: These experiments show that Nrp2WT and Nrp2C922S/C923S proteins display robust association with Golgi membranes, whereas the Nrp2TCS and Nrp2Full CS mutant proteins are significantly deficient in their association with the Golgi apparatus (Figure 3C, D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence and colocalization analysis shown in Figure 3C and 3D.

claim: Nrp2TCS and Nrp2Full CS mutant proteins are significantly deficient in their association with the Golgi apparatus.
source: These experiments show that Nrp2WT and Nrp2C922S/C923S proteins display robust association with Golgi membranes, whereas the Nrp2TCS and Nrp2Full CS mutant proteins are significantly deficient in their association with the Golgi apparatus (Figure 3C, D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence and colocalization analysis shown in Figure 3C and 3D.

claim: Nrp2TCS protein displays a markedly different trafficking pattern with a higher mobile fraction compared to Nrp2WT.
source: We observed that Nrp2TCS protein displays a markedly different trafficking pattern with a higher mobile fraction compared to Nrp2WT (Figure 3E and F; Videos 2 and 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by FRAP analysis shown in Figure 3E and 3F.

claim: Transmembrane/juxtamembrane palmitoyl acceptor Nrp2 cysteines are important for regulating the localization and trafficking of Nrp2 protein across subcellular compartments and the plasma membrane.
source: Taken together, these experiments support the functional importance of transmembrane/juxtamembrane palmitoyl acceptor Nrp2 cysteines in regulating the localization and trafficking of Nrp2 protein across subcellular compartments and the plasma membrane.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the localization, Golgi association, and FRAP experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: PlexA3 binds Nrp2Full CS to a similar extent as it does to Nrp2WT.
source: These experiments showed that PlexA3 binds Nrp2Full CS to a similar extent as it does to Nrp2WT (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by coimmunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4A and 4B.

claim: Exogenous Nrp2Full CS exhibits strong co-localization with endogenous PlexA3 in primary cortical neurons.
source: Further investigation into the association between palmitoylation-deficient Nrp2 and PlexA3 using immunofluorescence in primary cortical neurons in culture showed that exogenous Nrp2Full CS exhibits strong co-localization with endogenous PlexA3, similar to exogenously expressed Nrp2WT (Figure 3—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4C.

claim: The membrane-spanning and cytoplasmic Nrp2 cysteines are dispensable for the interaction between Nrp2 and PlexA3.
source: Thus, the membrane-spanning and cytoplasmic Nrp2 cysteines are dispensable for the interaction between Nrp2 and PlexA3.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the coimmunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4A-C.

claim: pHluorin-Nrp2Full CS associates with flag-Nrp2WT to a significantly lesser extent than pHuorin-Nrp2WT does.
source: These experiments revealed that pHluorin-Nrp2Full CS associates with flag-Nrp2WT to a significantly lesser extent than pHuorin-Nrp2WT does (Figure 3—figure supplement 4D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by coimmunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4D and 4E.

claim: pHluorin-Nrp2TCS associates with flag-Nrp2WT to a lesser extent than pHluorin-Nrp2WT does.
source: Moreover, coimmunoprecipitation experiments between flag-Nrp2WT and pHluorin-Nrp2WT or Nrp2TCS demonstrated that pHluorin-Nrp2TCS associates with flag-Nrp2WT to a lesser extent than pHluorin-Nrp2WT does (Figure 3—figure supplement 4F and G), although this difference is not as robust as it is with Nrp2Full CS.
evidence: This claim is supported by coimmunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4F and 4G.

claim: The Nrp2 cysteine residues that are palmitoylated and required for Nrp2 localization are also necessary for Nrp2 homo-oligomerization.
source: These findings show that the Nrp2 cysteine residues that we have shown to be palmitoylated and required for Nrp2 localization are also necessary for Nrp2 homo-oligomerization.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the coimmunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4D-G.

claim: Nrp2WT and Nrp2C922S/C923S can rescue the Nrp2 mutant dendritic spine phenotype in vitro.
source: These experiments show that Nrp2WT and Nrp2C922S/C923S can rescue the Nrp2 mutant dendritic spine phenotype (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by rescue experiments in Nrp2-/- cortical neurons shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: Nrp2C878S and Nrp2C887S are not capable of constraining spine number in Nrp2-/- cortical neurons.
source: In contrast, Nrp2C878S and Nrp2C887S are not capable of constraining spine number, whereas Nrp2C885S and Nrp2C897S can partially rescue the Nrp2 knockout dendritic spine phenotype (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by rescue experiments in Nrp2-/- cortical neurons shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: Nrp2C885S and Nrp2C897S can partially rescue the Nrp2 knockout dendritic spine phenotype in vitro.
source: In contrast, Nrp2C878S and Nrp2C887S are not capable of constraining spine number, whereas Nrp2C885S and Nrp2C897S can partially rescue the Nrp2 knockout dendritic spine phenotype (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by rescue experiments in Nrp2-/- cortical neurons shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: Transmembrane/juxtamembrane cysteines, but not the two C-terminal cysteines, are required for Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent dendritic spine pruning in vitro.
source: Likewise, Nrp2 mutant rescue experiments in cortical neuron cultures with pHluorin-tagged Nrp2WT or Nrp2CS mutant expression plasmids including the Nrp2TCS, Nrp2C922S/C923S, and Nrp2Full CS mutants, reveal a requirement for transmembrane/juxtamembrane cysteines, but not for the two C-terminal cysteines, in Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent dendritic spine pruning (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by rescue experiments in Nrp2-/- cortical neurons shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Sema3F application enhances Nrp2 palmitoylation in deep layer primary cortical neurons in culture.
source: Interestingly, Sema3F application enhances Nrp2 palmitoylation in deep layer primary cortical neurons in culture (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by ABE assay data shown in Figure 4E and 4F.

claim: Sema3F effects on cortical neurons are mediated by Nrp2 palmitoylation.
source: This shows that Sema3F can upregulate Nrp2 palmitoylation, presumably at nearby subcellular domains and within dendritic spines, and it further suggests that Sema3F effects on cortical neurons are mediated by Nrp2 palmitoylation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Sema3F enhances Nrp2 palmitoylation shown in Figure 4E and 4F.

claim: Neurons electroporated with Nrp2WT showed significantly fewer spines compared to Nrp2-/- neurons in vivo.
source: Neurons electroporated with the combination expressing Nrp2WT showed significantly fewer spines compared to Nrp2-/- neurons that do not express Nrp2 (electroporated with [Cre+LSL-tdTomato+EGFP]).
evidence: This claim is supported by in utero electroporation rescue experiments shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claim: Neurons electroporated with Nrp2TCS exhibited a spine density similar to that of Nrp2-/- neurons in vivo.
source: However, neurons electroporated with the combination of plasmids that includes Nrp2TCS exhibited a spine density similar to that of Nrp2-/- neurons (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by in utero electroporation rescue experiments shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claim: Transmembrane and membrane-proximal Nrp2 cysteines are essential for mediating Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent spine pruning in layer V cortical pyramidal neurons in vivo.
source: Taken together, both in vitro and in vivo rescue experiments of the Nrp2-/- dendritic spine density phenotype reveal an essential role for the transmembrane and membrane-proximal Nrp2 cysteines in mediating Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent spine pruning in layer V cortical pyramidal neurons.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the in vitro and in vivo rescue experiments shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: In Zdhhc15-KO cortical neurons overall Nrp2 palmitoylation is substantially reduced (~50%) compared to that in wild-type neurons.
source: In Zdhhc15-KO cortical neurons overall Nrp2 palmitoylation is substantially reduced (~50%) compared to that in wild-type neurons (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by ABE assay data shown in Figure 6A and 6B.

claim: Nrp1 palmitoylation in Zdhhc15-KO neurons is comparable to that observed in wild-type neurons.
source: Unlike Nrp2, Nrp1 palmitoylation in Zdhhc15-KO neurons is comparable to that observed in wild-type neurons (Figure 6A and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ABE assay data shown in Figure 6A and 6C.

claim: Nrp2 palmitoylation levels in Zdhhc8-/- cortical neurons are very close to those observed in wild-type cortical neurons.
source: Nrp2 palmitoylation levels in Zdhhc8-/- cortical neurons are very close to those observed in wild-type cortical neurons (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B) and, therefore, Nrp2 does not appear to be a palmitoyl substrate of ZDHHC8 in these neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by ABE assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and 1B.

claim: Nrp2 does not appear to be a palmitoyl substrate of ZDHHC8 in cortical neurons.
source: Nrp2 palmitoylation levels in Zdhhc8-/- cortical neurons are very close to those observed in wild-type cortical neurons (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B) and, therefore, Nrp2 does not appear to be a palmitoyl substrate of ZDHHC8 in these neurons.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the ABE assay data in Zdhhc8-/- neurons shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and 1B.

claim: Wild-type cortical neurons exhibit significant Sema3F-induced spine retraction.
source: Note that WT neurons exhibit significant Sema3F-induced spine retraction, whereas Zdhhc15-KO neurons invariably display no response to Sema3F-AP (compared to AP).
evidence: This claim is supported by dendritic spine density data shown in Figure 6D and 6E.

claim: Zdhhc15-KO neurons invariably display no response to Sema3F-AP in terms of spine retraction.
source: Note that WT neurons exhibit significant Sema3F-induced spine retraction, whereas Zdhhc15-KO neurons invariably display no response to Sema3F-AP (compared to AP).
evidence: This claim is supported by dendritic spine density data shown in Figure 6D and 6F.

claim: Zdhhc8-/- cortical neurons responded to Sema3F with significant spine retraction.
source: Zdhhc8-/- cortical neurons responded to Sema3F with significant spine retraction (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C and D), similar to wild-type cortical neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by dendritic spine density data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C and 1D.

claim: Both wild-type and Zdhhc15-KO cortical neurons exhibit a more elaborate perisomatic dendritic arbor following Sema3A-AP treatment compared to AP treatment.
source: Both WT and Zdhhc15-KO cortical neurons exhibit a more elaborate perisomatic dendritic arbor following Sema3A-AP treatment compared to AP (control) treatment.
evidence: This claim is supported by Sholl analysis data shown in Figure 6G-I.

claim: ZDHHC15 plays essential roles in Nrp2 palmitoylation and Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent dendritic spine pruning in primary deep layer cortical neurons.
source: These biochemical and phenotypic experiments in vitro reveal that ZDHHC15 plays essential roles in Nrp2 palmitoylation and Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent dendritic spine pruning, and that ZDHHC15 is dispensable for Nrp1 palmitoylation and Sema3A/Nrp1-dependent basal dendritic elaboration in primary deep layer cortical neurons.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the biochemical and phenotypic data shown in Figure 6.

claim: ZDHHC15 is dispensable for Nrp1 palmitoylation and Sema3A/Nrp1-dependent basal dendritic elaboration in primary deep layer cortical neurons.
source: These biochemical and phenotypic experiments in vitro reveal that ZDHHC15 plays essential roles in Nrp2 palmitoylation and Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent dendritic spine pruning, and that ZDHHC15 is dispensable for Nrp1 palmitoylation and Sema3A/Nrp1-dependent basal dendritic elaboration in primary deep layer cortical neurons.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the biochemical and phenotypic data shown in Figure 6.

claim: There is exquisite specificity among PATs for their neuronal substrates.
source: These results underscore the exquisite specificity among PATs for their neuronal substrates.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the differential effects of ZDHHC15 on Nrp2 versus Nrp1 shown in Figure 6.

claim: Zdhhc15-KO apical dendrites harbor more dendritic spines compared to wild-type neurons in layer V cortical pyramidal neurons labeled with the Thy1-EGFP-m line.
source: Our analysis of apical dendritic spines in wild-type and Zdhhc15-KO layer V cortical pyramidal neurons labeled with the Thy1-EGFP-m line shows that Zdhhc15-KO apical dendrites harbor more dendritic spines compared to wild-type neurons (Figure 7A and B), phenocopying previously observed effects of Nrp2 loss-of-function in this same neuronal population in vivo (Tran et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by dendritic spine density data shown in Figure 7A and 7B.

claim: Zdhhc15-KO layer V cortical pyramidal neurons phenocopy previously observed effects of Nrp2 loss-of-function in this same neuronal population in vivo.
source: Our analysis of apical dendritic spines in wild-type and Zdhhc15-KO layer V cortical pyramidal neurons labeled with the Thy1-EGFP-m line shows that Zdhhc15-KO apical dendrites harbor more dendritic spines compared to wild-type neurons (Figure 7A and B), phenocopying previously observed effects of Nrp2 loss-of-function in this same neuronal population in vivo (Tran et al., 2009).
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the dendritic spine density data shown in Figure 7A and 7B and comparison to prior work (Tran et al., 2009).

claim: There is no difference in dendritic arbor complexity between wild-type and Zdhhc15-KO layer V cortical pyramidal neurons in Golgi-stained brains.
source: Next, given the lack of an effect of ZDHHC15 on Nrp1 palmitoylation and function, we assessed the Sema3A/Nrp1-dependent basal dendritic arbor elaboration in Golgi-stained wild-type and Zdhhc15-KO brains and observed no difference in dendritic arbor complexity between wild-type and Zdhhc15-KO layer V cortical pyramidal neurons (Figure 7C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by Sholl analysis data shown in Figure 7C and 7D.

claim: Individual neurons in transheterozygous Nrp2 and Zdhhc15 mutant mice display a higher density of dendritic spines on the apical dendrite of deep layer cortical pyramidal neurons compared to single Nrp2 or Zdhhc15 heterozygotes.
source: Despite the shortcomings of this experiment, we observed that individual neurons in transheterozygous Nrp2 and Zdhhc15 mutant mice display a higher density of dendritic spines on the apical dendrite of deep layer cortical pyramidal neurons compared to single Nrp2 or Zdhhc15 heterozygotes (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic interaction data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C and 1D.

claim: Nrp2 and ZDHHC15 function in the same signaling pathway in vivo.
source: These observations are in line with our biochemical and phenotypic experiments presented here and support the hypothesis that Nrp2 and ZDHHC15 function in the same signaling pathway in vivo.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the genetic interaction data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C and 1D.

claim: Zdhhc15-deficient mice have an intact anterior commissure.
source: Analysis of wild-type and Zdhhc15-KO brains using neurofilament staining revealed an intact AC in Zdhhc15-deficient mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E), with none of the hallmark AC defects known to be present in Nrp2 mutants (Chen et al., 2000; Giger et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by neurofilament staining data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Zdhhc15-KO embryos show normal development and guidance of cranial nerves.
source: Likewise, the examination of Zdhhc15-KO embryos with whole-mount neurofilament staining revealed normal development and guidance of cranial nerves (data not shown).
evidence: This claim is stated but data is not shown.

claim: Select palmitoylated Nrp2 cysteines play a critical role in Nrp2 subcellular localization and function in deep layer cortical neurons.
source: Taken together, our in vitro and in vivo data suggest a critical role for select palmitoylated Nrp2 cysteines in Nrp2 subcellular localization and function in deep layer cortical neurons.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the comprehensive experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: PAT-substrate specificity drives diversification of Nrp2 and Nrp1 palmitoyl substrates to control deep layer cortical pyramidal neuron morphology.
source: Further, they reveal that PAT-substrate specificity drives diversification of Nrp2 and Nrp1 palmitoyl substrates to control deep layer cortical pyramidal neuron morphology and, presumably, neural circuit assembly.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the comprehensive experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Nrp2 and Nrp1 are novel neuronal palmitoylation substrates.
source: We show here that Nrp2 and Nrp1 are novel neuronal palmitoylation substrates and that select palmitoyl acceptor Nrp2 cysteines are critical for Nrp2 protein subcellular localization, for plasma membrane clustering and for Sema3F/Nrp2-dependent apical dendritic spine pruning in deep layer cortical pyramidal neurons in vitro and in vivo (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings supported by the experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Palmitoylation conveys upon Nrp2 a highly clustered localization pattern on the cell surface.
source: Specifically, palmitoylation conveys upon Nrp2, a highly clustered localization pattern on the cell surface, whereas Nrp1 is diffusely localized on the plasma membrane regardless of its palmitoylation state.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the localization data shown in Figures 1 and 3.

claim: Nrp1 is diffusely localized on the plasma membrane regardless of its palmitoylation state.
source: Specifically, palmitoylation conveys upon Nrp2, a highly clustered localization pattern on the cell surface, whereas Nrp1 is diffusely localized on the plasma membrane regardless of its palmitoylation state.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the localization data shown in Figures 1 and 3.

claim: Palmitoylation endows Nrp2 and Nrp1 with distinct functional properties that allow these receptors to exert their well-defined and distinct effects on cortical layer V pyramidal neuron morphogenesis.
source: These observations show that palmitoylation endows Nrp2 and Nrp1 with distinct functional properties that allow these receptors to exert their well-defined and distinct effects on cortical layer V pyramidal neuron morphogenesis.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the comprehensive experimental data showing differential effects of palmitoylation on Nrp2 versus Nrp1.

claim: The C-terminal Nrp2 di-cysteine motif CCXXX* does not appear to play essential roles in Nrp2 localization on Golgi membranes, cell surface compartmentalization, or dendritic spine pruning.
source: We find that the C-terminal Nrp2 di-cysteine motif CCXXX* ('*' denotes a stop codon) does not appear to play essential roles in Nrp2 localization on Golgi membranes, cell surface compartmentalization, or dendritic spine pruning, though minor effects of these cysteines can be observed in certain localization assays.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the experimental data on Nrp2C922S/C923S mutant shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: The juxtamembrane cysteines predominate over the C-terminal cysteines in regulating Nrp2 subcellular localization.
source: Taken together, these experiments support the functional importance of transmembrane/juxtamembrane palmitoyl acceptor Nrp2 cysteines in regulating the localization and trafficking of Nrp2 protein across subcellular compartments and the plasma membrane.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the comparative analysis of different Nrp2 CS mutants shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Bulk Nrp2 palmitoylation occurs on Golgi membranes.
source: Our observation that Nrp2 distribution includes localization in the Golgi apparatus suggests that bulk Nrp2 palmitoylation occurs on Golgi membranes, and that palmitoylated Nrp2 enters the post-Golgi secretory pathway to undergo anterograde trafficking toward the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is inferred from the Golgi localization data shown in Figure 3C-D and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Palmitoylated Nrp2 enters the post-Golgi secretory pathway to undergo anterograde trafficking toward the plasma membrane.
source: Our observation that Nrp2 distribution includes localization in the Golgi apparatus suggests that bulk Nrp2 palmitoylation occurs on Golgi membranes, and that palmitoylated Nrp2 enters the post-Golgi secretory pathway to undergo anterograde trafficking toward the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is inferred from the Golgi localization data shown in Figure 3C-D and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Nrp2 may be palmitoylated locally in dendrites in response to stimuli including its ligand Sema3F.
source: Interestingly, a significant fraction of Nrp2 protein is associated with Golgi membranes in dendrites of cortical neurons (Figure 3C and D and Figure 3—figure supplement 3), known as Golgi outposts (Horton et al., 2005). This suggests that Nrp2 may also be palmitoylated locally in response to stimuli including its ligand Sema3F, other signaling effectors or even neuronal activity, and that Nrp2 is then delivered to dendritic spines and synapses in response to these cues, as has been observed for other proteins (Noritake et al., 2009).
evidence: This is speculated based on the presence of Nrp2 in dendritic Golgi outposts and the observation that Sema3F enhances Nrp2 palmitoylation.

claim: The enhancement of Nrp2 palmitoylation by exposure to exogenous Sema3F may lead to rapid and/or controlled delivery of Nrp2 to synaptic sites.
source: Therefore, the enhancement we observe of Nrp2 palmitoylation by exposure to exogenous Sema3F (Figure 4E and F) may lead to rapid and/or controlled delivery of Nrp2 to synaptic sites.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation that Sema3F enhances Nrp2 palmitoylation shown in Figure 4E and 4F.

claim: Nrp2 and its ligand Sema3F are dynamically regulated in response to alterations in neuronal activity.
source: Moreover, Nrp2 and its ligand Sema3F are dynamically regulated in response to alterations in neuronal activity (Lee et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2017); in the case of Nrp2 this may in part be controlled by rapid cycles of Nrp2 palmitoylation-depalmitoylation in the vicinity of individual dendritic spines, a mechanism that can confer both spatial and temporal precision of protein localization and function (Fivaz and Meyer, 2003; Fukata et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated based on citations to prior work (Lee et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2017) and speculation about the role of palmitoylation cycles.

claim: Substrate specificity is a major determinant of the functional specification of cues that can regulate neuronal architecture and polarity.
source: The spatial and temporal organization of the palmitoylation network is largely governed by the precise spatiotemporal regulation of PATs (Greaves and Chamberlain, 2011; Noritake et al., 2009; Ohno et al., 2006), rendering substrate specificity a major determinant of the functional specification of cues that can regulate neuronal architecture and polarity.
evidence: This is stated based on citations to prior work and the experimental findings in this manuscript.

claim: Palmitoylation deficits lead to altered neuronal excitability and aberrant neuronal phenotypes linked to neural diseases.
source: Of note, there is increasing evidence that palmitoylation deficits lead to altered neuronal excitability and aberrant neuronal phenotypes linked to neural diseases (Mansouri et al., 2005; Milnerwood et al., 2013; Mukai et al., 2015; Mukai et al., 2008; Mukai et al., 2004; Pinner et al., 2016; Raymond et al., 2007; Singaraja et al., 2011; Sutton et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated based on citations to prior work.

claim: ZDHHC15 has been implicated in X-linked intellectual disability.
source: In particular ZDHHC15, shown here to play essential roles in Nrp2 palmitoylation and function, has been implicated in X-linked intellectual disability (Lewis et al., 2021; Mansouri et al., 2005), impairments in learning and memory (Wang et al., 2015), hyperactivity associated with a novel environment and sensitivity to psychostimulants (Mejias et al., 2021), and also dendritic outgrowth and formation of mature spines in hippocampal neurons in vitro (Shah et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated based on citations to prior work (Lewis et al., 2021; Mansouri et al., 2005).

claim: ZDHHC15 has been implicated in impairments in learning and memory.
source: In particular ZDHHC15, shown here to play essential roles in Nrp2 palmitoylation and function, has been implicated in X-linked intellectual disability (Lewis et al., 2021; Mansouri et al., 2005), impairments in learning and memory (Wang et al., 2015), hyperactivity associated with a novel environment and sensitivity to psychostimulants (Mejias et al., 2021), and also dendritic outgrowth and formation of mature spines in hippocampal neurons in vitro (Shah et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated based on citation to prior work (Wang et al., 2015).

claim: ZDHHC15 has been implicated in hyperactivity associated with a novel environment and sensitivity to psychostimulants.
source: In particular ZDHHC15, shown here to play essential roles in Nrp2 palmitoylation and function, has been implicated in X-linked intellectual disability (Lewis et al., 2021; Mansouri et al., 2005), impairments in learning and memory (Wang et al., 2015), hyperactivity associated with a novel environment and sensitivity to psychostimulants (Mejias et al., 2021), and also dendritic outgrowth and formation of mature spines in hippocampal neurons in vitro (Shah et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated based on citation to prior work (Mejias et al., 2021).

claim: ZDHHC15 has been implicated in dendritic outgrowth and formation of mature spines in hippocampal neurons in vitro.
source: In particular ZDHHC15, shown here to play essential roles in Nrp2 palmitoylation and function, has been implicated in X-linked intellectual disability (Lewis et al., 2021; Mansouri et al., 2005), impairments in learning and memory (Wang et al., 2015), hyperactivity associated with a novel environment and sensitivity to psychostimulants (Mejias et al., 2021), and also dendritic outgrowth and formation of mature spines in hippocampal neurons in vitro (Shah et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated based on citation to prior work (Shah et al., 2019).

claim: Sema3F/Nrp2 signaling plays important roles in hippocampal circuit function.
source: Intriguingly, Sema3F/Nrp2 signaling has been shown to play important roles in hippocampal circuit function, and its dysregulation may cause epileptic activity in mice (Eisenberg et al., 2021; Li et al., 2022; Sahay et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated based on citations to prior work (Eisenberg et al., 2021; Li et al., 2022; Sahay et al., 2005).

claim: Dysregulation of Sema3F/Nrp2 signaling may cause epileptic activity in mice.
source: Intriguingly, Sema3F/Nrp2 signaling has been shown to play important roles in hippocampal circuit function, and its dysregulation may cause epileptic activity in mice (Eisenberg et al., 2021; Li et al., 2022; Sahay et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated based on citations to prior work (Eisenberg et al., 2021; Li et al., 2022; Sahay et al., 2005).

claim: Neuropilins are key players in cancer growth and progression and response to antineoplastic therapies.
source: Moreover, neuropilins are key players in cancer growth and progression and response to antineoplastic therapies (Napolitano and Tamagnone, 2019; Rizzolio and Tamagnone, 2011), and they also play important roles in the function of the immune system (Kumanogoh and Kikutani, 2013) and the vascular system (Gu et al., 2003; Simons et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated based on citations to prior work (Napolitano and Tamagnone, 2019; Rizzolio and Tamagnone, 2011).

claim: Neuropilins play important roles in the function of the immune system.
source: Moreover, neuropilins are key players in cancer growth and progression and response to antineoplastic therapies (Napolitano and Tamagnone, 2019; Rizzolio and Tamagnone, 2011), and they also play important roles in the function of the immune system (Kumanogoh and Kikutani, 2013) and the vascular system (Gu et al., 2003; Simons et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated based on citation to prior work (Kumanogoh and Kikutani, 2013).

claim: Neuropilins play important roles in the function of the vascular system.
source: Moreover, neuropilins are key players in cancer growth and progression and response to antineoplastic therapies (Napolitano and Tamagnone, 2019; Rizzolio and Tamagnone, 2011), and they also play important roles in the function of the immune system (Kumanogoh and Kikutani, 2013) and the vascular system (Gu et al., 2003; Simons et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated based on citations to prior work (Gu et al., 2003; Simons et al., 2016).

claim: DHHC enzyme-substrate specificity is a novel mechanism specifying the functional identity of neuronal substrates.
source: Our experiments identify neuropilins as new members of the neuronal palmitoyl proteome, reveal new DHHC enzymatic substrates in the CNS, and define DHHC enzyme-substrate specificity as a novel mechanism specifying the functional identity of neuronal substrates.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the comprehensive experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: These results advance our understanding of CNS development and function.
source: These results advance our understanding of CNS development and function and may prove invaluable for the development of targeted therapeutic approaches directed toward amelioration of neural disorders associated with aberrant function of palmitoylation signaling pathways.
evidence: This is a concluding statement about the significance of the findings.
